no_loosening.method: every attempt's answer from both arms, validated by the base commit's SelectionPlan and by the candidate's

not_covered: Whether the right plan finds the right photograph: retrieval, the text join and the packet are not exercised. Only the plan is scored.
The plan's limit is not scored, so a right plan with a null query and a limit of one may still hand the composer the wrong photograph at a place with several.
The composer and the answer a person reads.
Any model but the structured-extraction primary, any language but English, and catalogues larger than eleven entities.
Questions naming a place that is not saved, or naming two places.
Real personal data: every name is invented.

candidate_change: The first experiment's candidate, unchanged: the client's refusal names the schema's reasons; the content selection's refusals say where a search for anything visible or written belongs; the planner prompt selection-6.

exulanica/selection/question.py _without_placeholders: removes from the semantic query every placeholder this request assigned, in any case, with or without brackets. Derived from the placeholders the request assigned rather than from a list of class words, so ordinary text that only resembles one is kept.
exulanica/selection/question.py propose_plan: a reply cut off at the token limit is asked for once more, within the same two attempts; a second cut-off is raised as before.
notes.development_smoke_test: The development split, used only as a smoke test: 100 of 100 right, no repair, no error.
deviations: None in procedure. The runs, the scorer and the gates are as pre-registered.
findings: S-P12, 'What's on the menu at Cinder Lane Baths?': both arms chose the cross-content intent with scope related and no query in 5 of 5 draws. The plan is accepted, so nothing is refused, and it answers with a listing of what is related to the place rather than with what the menu says. The change does not reach this question; it is the one place question the candidate gets wrong, and the base commit gets it wrong the same way.

S-C02, 'What does the banner over the road say?': the base commit wrote 'banner over road text' in 5 of 5 draws; the candidate wrote 'banner over road' twice, 'banner road say' once and 'banner road' twice. The pre-registered scorer does not allow 'over', but PostgreSQL's English configuration drops it (measured on a throwaway server: 'banner over road' becomes the lexemes banner and road), so for retrieval those queries are the same as 'banner road'. 'say' is kept by that configuration. Read that way, the base commit is right in 5 of 5 and the candidate in 4 of 5. This reading is not a gate and was made after the numbers.
S-H08, 'Where have I photographed Tobias?': the base commit was right in 2 of 5 draws; the candidate in 5 of 5.
The candidate made no refusal, no repair and no truncated reply in any of its 140 draws, and no question scored lower on the candidate than on the base commit.
notes.latency_note: Wall milliseconds on a shared machine, niceness 0 on every run, arms alternated so both saw the same conditions. One-minute load average between 4.22 and 12.63 across the ten runs.

record.profile_note: Outcome of the pre-registered planner reliability experiment, scored once per arm on the held-out split. No model call is made to write it.
